% States the margin the per-query data actually support.
\paragraph{Verdict on H1.2.} H1.2 is supported only at a margin considerably wider than originally stated, and not uniformly. Under a paired TOST on per-query differences ($\theta = \varepsilon\,\mu_{\text{baseline}}$, $\alpha = 0.05$), BM25-sampled negatives are equivalent to expensively mined negatives in 901 of 1623 comparisons at $\varepsilon = 0.10$, but in only 25 at the $\varepsilon = 0.01$ margin stated in Section~4.2.5. The median smallest supported margin is $\varepsilon^{*} = 0.086$. On the TREC Deep Learning collections no comparison attains equivalence at $1\%$ in either year: with 43--54 queries, demonstrating a $1\%$ margin would require on the order of a thousand, so the in-domain claim is beyond the resolving power of the test collections rather than contradicted by them. The out-of-domain claim is the stronger of the two. The density-ratio analysis is unaffected: the operative factors remain teacher pairwise entropy and the essential diameter of the query manifold, and the effectiveness measurements themselves reproduce exactly.
